newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Interest rates rises will not hit HK banks - Lehman.
newsitem.headline: Interest rates rises will not hit HK banks - Lehman.

text.p: Interest rate rises would have no material impact on Hong Kong banks even though uncertainties over interest rates could suppress share prices, Lehman Brothers Asia said on Thursday.

There are fears that interest rate rises could dampen loan demand and lead to higher non-performing debt charges and a contraction of margins, senior regional banking analyst Raymond Lee told a news conference.
"Economic activity in Hong Kong is much more hinged on growth in China," he said.
Hong Kong's economy relies heavily on its economic ties with China, for which the territory serves as an entrepot and service centre.
Interest rate rises would not contract the margins of local banks because they have a large pool of free resources, Lee said.
And as Hong Kong companies have rather low debt gearing, interest rate rises are unlikely to lead to a higher level of non-performance debt, he added.
But uncertainties in interest rates do put pressure on the share prices of banking stocks amid ivnestors' fears, Lee said.
There are concerns that U.S. interest rates will rise. Hong Kong interest rates often move in tandem with their U.S. counterparts as the local currency is pegged to the U.S. unit.
